title: Reconciling global collaboration and data sovereignty in neuroscience
title_zh: 在神经科学中协调全球合作与数据主权
abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) elevates the economic and strategic value of data, governments are intensifying efforts to regulate the collection, use and cross-border transfer of personal information. Data are increasingly treated as national assets, subject to legal, economic and geopolitical controls. These shifts are reshaping scientific research, particularly in neuroscience and brain health, where progress depends on access to large, diverse and internationally distributed datasets. In parallel, advances in neuroimaging, neurotechnology and computational modeling are enabling population-scale neuroscience and the generation of AI-ready brain datasets. These developments further increase the strategic importance of neural data, amplifying both their scientific value and their governance complexity. The convergence of these trends exposes a fundamental tension between the need for an open science culture and data sovereignty. Without coordinated responses, these dynamics risk limiting representation, slowing innovation and reinforcing global inequities in brain health research. Here we argue that neuroscience requires an international data governance coordinating body capable of aligning research and regulatory priorities. In addition to outlining the distinct challenges posed by neural data, we propose strategies to support secure, equitable and sustainable global collaboration, as well as practical governance instruments to enable coordinated implementation across jurisdictions.
abstract_zh: 随着人工智能（AI）提升数据的经济和战略价值，各国政府正加强监管个人信息的收集、使用和跨境流动。数据日益被视为国家资产，受到法律、经济和地缘政治的控制。这些转变正在重塑科学研究，特别是在神经科学和脑健康领域，进展取决于获取大规模、多样化且国际分布的数据集。与此同时，神经成像、神经技术和计算建模的进步正在推动规模化神经科学和AI就绪型脑数据集的生成。这些进一步提高了神经数据的战略重要性，放大了其科学价值和治理复杂性。这些趋势的交汇暴露了开放科文化念与数据主权之间的根本张力。若缺乏协调的应对，这些动态可能会限制代表性、阻碍创新并加剧脑健康研究中的全球不平等。本文论证称，神经科学需要一个国际数据治理协调机构，以协调研究和监管优先事项。除阐述神经数据所面临的独特挑战外，我们还提出了支持安全、公平和可持续全球合作的策略，以及跨司法管辖区协调实施的实用治理工具。
